what: Three paths evicted the stores' pool pages in line on the daemon's loop, two of them with Store::evict_pool(u64::MAX) on both stores once a second while memory was short. In a cold build of tempo they were 68 spans, 1,605 s of wall for 90 s of CPU on the loop's thread, with turns of up to 542 s, during which the give-back ladder and the typed failure of a task that does not fit (both run once a turn) could not run.
cause: the pool's eviction had three callers, each sized by itself, and none bounded what one loop turn does
class: unbounded work in a turn of the one loop (rule 18); one concept in several homes (rule 30)
prevention: blaze_graph::poolgive::Slices is the one rule (a slice a turn, dry after two empty sweeps) and Jobs::sweep_pools its one driver; its simulation's oracle refuses a sweep past a slice and a sweep of dry pools, with both planted
fix: the pressure handler and the plot ask (Jobs::ask_pools); the ladder's pool rung asks; PoolGive::Unpinned is gone
state: fixed, not yet compiled or run by this lane (write-only); no daemon-simulation test, since the simulation's stores are pumped and give no page back
